prompt: Complete ColorToken, a static factory that caches one instance per normalised name so that of("  red ") and of("RED") return the very same object (==), with a clearCache for tests.
explanation: The cache is a static field, so it belongs to the class and is shared by every caller, while name is an instance field belonging to each token. Making the constructor private forces callers through of(...), which is what lets the factory decide whether to build a new object or hand back one it already made. Normalising the key before the lookup is what makes two differently spelled requests land on the same cached instance.
hints: The cache belongs to the class rather than to any instance, so declare it static and final, mapping the normalised name to the token, and initialise it where it is declared so it is created once with the class.
Normalise with trim() and toUpperCase() BEFORE you look in the map, and reject the key if it is empty.
Look the key up first: only call the private constructor when the map has no entry, then store what you built.
